lead: T4/T5 blockade gives the clearest qualitative match. HS loss is the more informative steering test, with a consistent right-sided deficit and a variable left-sided effect. LPLC2 silencing shows partial pathway agreement.
hs_qualification: The two sides are not equally convincing: right-HS loss reduced the raw rightward command in all 10 seeds; left-HS loss reduced the leftward command in 7 of 10 seeds, and its 95% seed interval includes no reduction. This uncertainty must remain visible in any manuscript claim.

studies.label: HS-cell loss
studies.result: Right-HS loss reduced the rightward raw steering command by 20.3%; left-HS loss reduced the leftward command by 15.8% on average. Opposite-direction raw commands were preserved. Left-sided effects varied substantially.
studies.judgment: Promising but mixed qualitative agreement. Most relevant to MP's steering question; a selective fruit-fly silencing assay is not identical to the historical blowfly microsurgery experiment.

studies.label: T4/T5 blockade
studies.result: Both directional steering gains fell to zero in every seed. The independently driven looming pathway remained unchanged.
studies.judgment: Clearest qualitative match to optomotor loss. Limited validation strength because T4/T5 are the directly driven motion inputs in this model.

studies.label: LPLC2 silencing
studies.result: Mean giant-fiber firing fell from 249.0 to 199.8 Hz, retaining 80.2% of the paired intact response. Jump and flight-power motor activity remained substantial.
studies.judgment: Partial pathway agreement. The test does not reproduce the size/velocity decomposition or loss of GF-mediated escape in the published animal assay.

recommendations: Keep all three results and every control in a supplementary pilot figure. Describe them as frozen-model qualitative consistency tests, with the source-to-model assay differences stated explicitly.

Prioritize the HS experiment for follow-up because it addresses MP's steering question. Show both sides, raw R/L/F commands and the uncertainty in left-HS effects. Increase the seed count and obtain a matched stimulus/readout comparison before promoting a broad validation claim.
Keep T4/T5 blockade as a basic input-pathway control. Its complete response loss alone gives limited evidence that the internal circuit dynamics are biologically accurate.

For the looming benchmark, introduce literature-grounded size/velocity input time courses and a corresponding GF temporal endpoint before comparing escape behavior. Retain the current residual activity and the different LC4/LPLC2 motor effects as limitations to investigate.

Do not retune the frozen model to make these three results look better. If model changes follow, document them separately and evaluate them on additional held-out experiments. These tests do not validate graft repair.
